title: Recommendations: what should we show next?
hook: Popular items, similar items, similar people, hybrids, or asking a language model.
inPlainWords: There are two kinds of clues: what an item is like, and what people like you did. Good systems mix both and plan for the visitor with no history.

useCase.title: Suggest products on the ShopEase home page
useCase.story: 50,000 products, 200,000 customers, and lots of clicks and orders. A brand-new visitor arrives with no history at all.

approaches.name: Content-based (similar items)
approaches.what: Recommend items like the ones you liked, using descriptions and tags.
approaches.greatWhen: New items, or thin behavior history.
approaches.example: You bought a blender, so here are similar blenders.

approaches.name: Collaborative (people like you)
approaches.greatWhen: You have lots of behavior data.
approaches.avoidWhen: New visitors or new items with no history. This is the cold-start problem.
approaches.example: Shoppers like you also bought a milk frother.

approaches.name: Hybrid
approaches.avoidWhen: A tiny catalog where "popular" is enough.
approaches.example: Popular now, similar to what you clicked, and what your look-alikes bought.

approaches.name: Ask a language model
approaches.what: Describe the shopper in words and ask a model to suggest items.
approaches.greatWhen: Conversational shopping, explanations, and a chat with a new visitor.
approaches.avoidWhen: Ranking at large scale. It is slower and costlier, and it may suggest things you do not stock.
approaches.example: "I need a gift for a runner under $50."

approaches.name: Business rules on top
approaches.what: Filter and re-rank for stock, margin and variety.

challenge.question: A brand-new visitor with no history arrives. What is the best home page approach?

options.why: There is nothing to compare this visitor with.

options.text: Popular items plus session clues, growing into a hybrid as history builds
options.why: It works on day one and improves as data arrives.
A safe start, but it never personalizes.

options.text: Let a model invent suggestions from nothing
options.why: It has no data on this visitor and may suggest items you do not sell.

bestCase.title: Start with popular and session clues, then grow into a hybrid
bestCase.example: A new visitor sees this week's top sellers. After clicking two running shoes, the page shows similar shoes. After three orders, behavior from look-alike customers joins in. Out-of-stock items are always hidden.

worstCase.title: One method that ignores the cold start
worstCase.example: Collaborative-only means a new visitor sees a blank shelf, and new products never appear because no one has bought them yet. Meanwhile an ungrounded model suggests a product you do not sell.

route.travelling: New visitor who just clicked two running shoes

steps.label: Gather clues
steps.goes: Two clicks in this session are all we have.
steps.goesWrong: Only collaborative filtering is used. There is no history, so nothing is shown.

steps.label: Candidate list
steps.goes: Popular items plus items similar to the shoes.

steps.label: Score and rank
steps.goes: Blend the clues. Behavior weighs in as history grows.

steps.label: Show and learn
steps.goes: Clicks feed the next round of suggestions.

takeaway: Recommendations mix what an item is like with what people like you did. Plan for the visitor with no history.
